Portland property tax is billed by the offices named below.

Who bills what in Portland

  • Multnomah County property tax office - handles values and tax collection handles assessment.
  • Multnomah County property tax office bills and collects the tax.

Due dates

Multnomah payment FAQ: payments due Nov 15 (next business day if weekend/holiday); 3% discount for full payment, 2% for 2/3 with final due May 15; 1/3 payment with Feb 15 and May 15 installments. A Multnomah news-release headline (search result only) states payments due Nov. 16, 2026.. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Petition to the Property Values Appeals Board (formerly BOPTA) must be postmarked or delivered by December 31 after the current-year tax statement is available; accepted by mail or in person only.. See the official page.

Tax rate

We could not confirm the current Portland rate on an opened page, so we do not state one.

Local notes

  • Appeals go first to the county Property Value Appeals Board (formerly Board of Property Tax Appeals, BOPTA), filed with the county clerk, then Oregon Tax Court Magistrate Division.
  • Census Vintage 2025 population 635109; primary county Multnomah County from Census SUMLEV 157.
  • City spans multiple counties (Multnomah County, Washington County, Clackamas County); the part of the city in each county is assessed and collected by that county. Only the primary county's offices were researched.

Portland by the numbers

Portland has roughly 642,715 residents in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, and ranks number 1 by population among the 27 or places in this guide. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $557,600 here, which is 20% above the middle figure for the 27 or places. About 47% of households rent, so 53% own; the or median for these places is 61% owner-occupied. Homes here were typically built in 1966, so the median house is about 57 years old. These numbers describe Portland as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.
